observation_summary: The FastDateFormat.format(Date) method produces incorrect week-of-year values because it initializes a GregorianCalendar using only the time zone, ignoring the locale-specific rules for the first day of the week and minimal days in the first week.
hypothesis: The root cause is that the GregorianCalendar instance used for formatting is initialized without the locale, causing it to default to the system's locale settings instead of the locale provided during FastDateFormat instantiation.
prediction: The fix will involve passing the mLocale field into the GregorianCalendar constructor within the format(Date) method.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff shows exactly this change: 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' was changed to 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'. This confirms that the initialization of the calendar object was missing the necessary locale parameter.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an incorrect initialization of a helper object (GregorianCalendar). The logic for formatting is correct, but the state of the calendar object used for the calculation is wrong because it was initialized with the wrong constructor parameters. This fits the definition of Assignment/Initialization.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The algorithm itself (formatting) is correct; the issue is that the data structure (Calendar) used by the algorithm was initialized with incorrect parameters.
This is a local procedural fix, not a design-level capability gap.
